name: Golem
dom: artificial life; protection; holy names; clay
note: An anthropoid of clay animated through the ritual permutation of Hebrew letters and divine names (the word emet/'truth'); Scholem traces the motif from Sefer Yetsirah speculation to the medieval Hasidei Ashkenaz and the later Prague-Maharal legend.

name: Dybbuk
dom: spirit possession; the restless dead; affliction
note: A malevolent clinging spirit (Hebrew dibbuq, 'attachment') of a dead person that possesses a living body and requires exorcism; the developed concept is early-modern (16th-17th c. Lurianic and East European folklore).

name: Ibbur
dom: soul impregnation; righteous indwelling; spiritual aid
note: The benevolent counterpart to the dybbuk: the temporary 'impregnation' (ibbur) of a living person by the soul of a righteous departed one to help complete a mitzvah; a Lurianic doctrine described by Scholem, distinct from gilgul (transmigration).

name: Estrie
dom: blood-drinking; shape-shifting; night; harm to infants
note: A shape-shifting, blood-drinking female demon of medieval (esp. Franco-German) Jewish folklore, attested chiefly in Sefer Hasidim; the name likely derives from the Latin strix/strigae and the figure is sparsely documented.

name: The Classes of the Jinn
dom: jinn taxonomy; classification of hidden beings
note: A grouping node for the ranked classes of jinn enumerated in classical Islamic lore (al-Jahiz, al-Damiri) — jinni, shaytan, ifrit, marid, ghul, si'lat and others; the roster and hierarchy differ between authors and are not Quranically fixed.

name: Shaytan / Shayatin
note: The shayatin are the devils, the rebellious and tempting class of evil spirits led by Iblis; the Qur'an repeatedly names al-shaytan as humanity's open enemy who whispers temptation.

name: Ghul
note: The ghul (English 'ghoul'), a shape-shifting desert demon of pre-Islamic Arabian and classical Islamic lore that lures and devours lone travellers, classed among the jinn but of marginal, debated status in orthodox cosmology.

name: Si'lat
note: The si'lat (or si'la), a cunning, often female class of jinn in classical Arabian lore, sometimes paired with or distinguished from the ghul; sparsely and inconsistently described.

name: Div
dom: malevolence; monstrous strength; opposition to heroes
note: The div (Persian dev), a malevolent demonic being of Persianate Islamic and pre-Islamic Iranian tradition (cf. the Avestan daeva), assimilated to the jinn in Islamic-era folklore and prominent in epics such as the Shahnameh.

name: Gog and Magog
dom: eschatological war; the final assault; the nations of the end
note: Gog of the land of Magog (Ezekiel 38-39), reinterpreted in Revelation 20:8 as 'Gog and Magog,' the nations gathered by Satan after the millennium for the final assault before their destruction by fire; modeled as a single paired eschatological entity.
